text:
Plenty in Ottawa had come with something other than the game on their minds. A protest had been planned over Alex Ovechkin's support for Vladimir Putin, and CBC's headline on his response quoted him: "Nobody's using me." By the end, Ovechkin had his name on the winning goal, an assist on Cole Hutson's overtime wrister 1:14 into the extra period, and the Capitals had a 3-2 win they didn't really deserve.

Ottawa was the better team for long stretches. The Senators had 70 shot attempts to Washington's 40 and owned the second period, 1.61 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 0.73. By our replay of every shot they won this 63% of the time. They also lost Nick Cousins, who left after a hit from Jakob Chychrun that drew no penalty and plenty of argument afterward.

Washington scored 35 seconds in, Matt Roy beating Samuel Ersson with a slap shot that had a 3% chance of going in. Ottawa took over from there. Ridly Greig tied it on a backhand midway through the second, and Hayden Hodgson, back from a two-game suspension for his hit on Brandt Clarke, put the Senators ahead at 16:04 with Thomas Chabot assisting on both goals. That lead lasted until 12:31 of the third, when Pierre-Luc Dubois scored off a feed from Hutson and Tom Wilson and moved the Capitals' win chance from 15% to 48%.

Then Hutson, the 2024 second-round pick, ended it. His overtime goal was a 6% chance and by our count added half a win, the most of anyone on the ice. Logan Thompson made 24 saves and was 0.85 goals better than expected. Ersson, at the other end, allowed three goals on 17 shots, almost a goal worse than expected, and that is the difference in a game Ottawa controlled. Neither power play scored, and Ottawa won 41 of 63 faceoffs.

Ovechkin has one goal in his first 15 games, a slow start Daily Faceoff has been tracking. Tuesday he did his work as a passer. The Senators will want to know how Cousins is; they'll want back the point they left on the table even more.
headline: Hutson wins it in Ottawa on a night that wasn't about hockey
